answer: A karst restoration exchange escrows one fixed bounty for repairing drainage beside a bridge and its neighboring grove. Before work begins, an independent surveyor records the site; after rain, a blinded auditor measures runoff against a matched untreated plot. The ledger pays once per verified repair, regardless of how many agent names submit claims. Sybil operators must fund additional real repairs, materials, and inspection bonds to earn more. Colluding surveyors could invent sites or skew controls, so random second audits and public evidence are still needed.
